ques: It seems (if I don't misinterpret what I read here) that you write lyrics and music simultaneously. Question 1. Do you do like Paul McCartney and write mumbly lyrics and then refine them? Or is it more a bit by bit approach? Question 2. Have you ever tried to write music to some existing text? If yes, can you describe the problems you encountered?
answ: like a warning light on your car, the songwriting vehicle has this little light on the dashboard that warns you: "ATTENTION, AS OF APPROXIMATELY 2 SECONDS AGO, YOUR MELODY GOT AHEAD OF THE WORDS. SO IF YOU ARE WONDERING WHY YOUR CAR IS NOW SPUTTERING TO A HALT,... IT'S CAUSE YOUR MELODY GOT AHEAD OF THE WORDS" and the same thing happens when the words get too far ahead of the melody. THe strongest confluence of real power seems to happen when it's just all flying together, except maybe with the words like a nano second ahead, like you get maybe 7 words with no melody at all but within nano seconds the melody swoops in for it. That's usually when i get the strongest results. HOWEVER, for variety's sake it is very important to let it happen all kinds of other different ways. including entire melodies first or entire lines of words first. Sometimes the first thing i get is actually like a whole section of melody (such as the entire main melody for 'meet me in september'). Other times the first thing i get is a long line of prose (such as "i like to wear soft clothing cuz it makes me feel like i'm rough in comparison", or even "not very much money grows on trees anymore cuz we burned them all down" which i dont remember if it was actually words first but it sounds like the kind of line that would be)

ques: i cant believe this is the FIRST song u did with no click. i have a band and we recorded 1 song with click and decided it just didnt vibe with us. did u use click because u liked it or just because its how youre supposed to do it
answ: i can't seem to answer this in less than a million words. this is my third try. For a band, for sure, it's always been clear to me that to take full advantage of a live band you gotta ditch the click. But when you're just 1 person, and you're doing all the parts yourself, separately,.... i've always gone with the assumption that to pull this off you kinda need a click in there from the beginning, to act as like scaffolding. But something came over me recently and on a curiosity binge i started testing to see who else has used clicks over the years, and it was like this whole subject opened up that i had ALMOST thought about before, but wasnt ready to really consider, as a 1-person band. I can't believe it either, but this might be the first time i really, seriously considered what you really have to gain by staying off the click. and it became fascinating to pick out which songs and artists, especially ones from that middle time period where the click was gradually starting to catch on to everyone, (with guitar bands succumbing to it last, finally as everyone moved onto protools or whatever) it became really fun to check the ones where i was 50/50 not sure whether they would have used it. And to start really thinking about what that does for the song. It was particularly fascinating to realize, so often, for the songs that didnt use click track, i found that on some level i secretly already knew. already knew the tempo fluctuates a little in those spots. Anyway, i kept checking these songs for clicks and was basically foaming at the mouth with the desire to try going off click, but i still wasnt sure it would be possible for a 1-person band. But there was 1 album left to check, actually 2, because two seperate artists came to mind, both of whom did their first solo album entirely by themselves. one in 1995 and the other in 1970. and so, before i even checked to see if they used a click, i made a deal with myself: if i find out that BOTH of these guys, doing solo albums by themselves, were able to do it without a click, then i would officially have no excuse. i was honestly expecting they would have a click, but secretly hoping they might not. well my wish came true

ques: Do you really believe that we know why our passions are able to envigour such powerful emotions within us? The chill when a lush chord change hits or the shiver and awe of the howl of a perfectly mechanically balanced even firing V10, the thrill and intrigue of creating and consuming art. It doesn't feel like pure biology. It doesn't feel like a pre programmed drive. It's bigger than the love that pertains to relationships, which is biologically superficial with so much intensity that many believe its the most beautiful thing about being alive. In my opinion its the most powerful illusion. The fact that we can feel so strongly about something that has no evolutionary necessity is how we differ from animals. It is what creates individuality. It is what drives human progress. Passion is the most powerful aspect about being alive as a human being.
answ: i'm not so convined that other animals dont have it, and i'm not so convinced that it has 'no evolutionary necessity' as you say. but to answer your first question, no i do not believe that we really know exactly what it's all about. ques: Bill something i've been thinking about a lot is how can all art be perfect *and* always have room for improvement *and* nothing be perfect *at the same time*??? Like someone will tell me my art is perfect and like, yeah, okay, i made it it's something i created from my own brain and that's valuable or whatever etc, but i'm also like, No!! That's not be true!! It can't be!!! It's literally impossible!!!! Thoughts on this please, thabks!
answ: this all just comes down to a word problem. Language is fun and extremely useful, for sure, but in terms of rigid accuracy, it's never gonna hold up to the nuance of infinitely complex reality. My understanding of 'perfect' is it implies only 1 totally correct result. And the only types of assignments i can think of that could have just 1 answer are non-creative assignments. Make a totally straight line. Make perfect silence. Pitch black. Solid white. Or if the assignment is to perfectly copy an image, there is 1 correct answer which is to make exactly the same image. If the goal is to imagine something, with creativity, then you don't have this single-best-answer, you actually have infinite answers that are, actually, infinitely good. Could you still use 'perfect' somewhere in here? maybe, and words always morph and change over time, because they were never fully accurate to begin with, but for now i think 'perfect' is not even a relevant concept in the field of creativity. kind of like how the Richter scale is not useful for measuring rainfall

ques: does "not very much money grows on trees anymore, cause we burnt them all down" relate to trees getting burned constantly? cuz money = green, leaves = green. also is the meaning of in the future that someone believes that the world in the future will be like a dystopia
answ: let's sort this out. the verses have dystopian vibes, definitely not in a miserable way but in a groovy way. like a halloween costume, those things are not supposed to make anyone miserable, they are certainly for parties. ok so that's the surreal dystopian desert groove vibe, for all the verses. a lot of paradoxes in the verses too, i took great care to evoke things that seem unusual and/or impossible, also a lot of opposites thrown around, throughout the verses. Ok so that's the verses. Then, there's this long string of other parts which we'll call the "B section", and in those parts a lot more unfolds. At "when is it?" it abruptly without warning becomes incredibly eager and excited, like an excited child asking "are we there yet?" when they are excited to go to the water park for their birthday and just can't wait. then from "how am i supposed", the emotional investment comes out, we deeply care and know there's a lot to know but we're wondering how we're gonna know it. Then from "know what this means to you", it intimately acknowledges the stakes, alluding to the intimacy being in this together, acknowledging that we know "you" and "i" both care about this (while not specifying if that means we care about the same or different things or some other combination). "in the future i believe" (first occurence) is a statement of confidence, but then the meaning twists slightly because the line lengthens unexpectedly to "in the future i believe things go a little differently", which to me evokes intrigue, innovation, optimism, differentness. sorry for saying evoke twice. sidenote, "different" is one of my top all time favorite concepts to bring up in music because it's exactly 50/50 that it means good or bad. so that leaves it actually up to the music to help you decide what you think that word inherently means in that moment. Ok so then with the "things i want to see" part, is like youre pleading about some things you've been desperately waiting for the chance to get to see, or find out, in the future. Then "when's the future gonna be?" is more eagerness, but with a dreamy/awe sort of sound to it in the music. like dreamingly anticipating and wondering when it's gonna be. then "IN THE FUTURE, I BELIEVE" is the climactic line and what could be considered the real title line. To me this is the most important statement of the song, the 'conclusion' of the song, the 'motto' of the song, etc, and i take it to mean "i believe in the future." However, as a diagnosed double meanings junkie, i confess to also being very glad that there is technically a double meaning opportunity here, because it could be like "When's the future gonna be? [checks watch] oh, that will be ... in the future, i believe." The third verse goes right back into groovy surreal dystopian desert, like before, and basically just repeats the whole form. Some tiny lyric swaps here and there for the second B section, but it pretty much hits all the same emotional beats as the first. Then after that's all done, there's that 1-liner ejectorseat ending thing i like to do, based on the opening, and in this case it just mentions a bit of timetravel mechanics, and a reference to the only possible way that we all know how to get to the future, which is simply via the passage of time. is it better now that i've explained it

In "2 friends on the beach", i was reasonable and i put all 4 locations in different project files. but in 2023 i was feeling so greedy about everything, including the fact that i started doing 10 videos at the same time, and so not only did i insist on putting scenes from 2 different towns in the same contiguous physical space (actually seperated by their accurate real world distance which was maybe about a mile), IN ADDITION because i was doing 10 videos at a time, i made that mistake at least twice (in different videos) without fully realizing the consequences. The consequences, as i eventually figured out, is when you have things too far from the center, especially with very very small things, they wobble. it's like the resolution of how precise their vertices can be is reduced, so they wobble around. Anyway, after spending the last 24 hours thinking about how to solve this, i finally was able to safely and surgically program something that actually moves the whole world for one scene and then moves it again for the other scene, without messing anything up. Which will also work fine for the other video, but if i didn't have the programming experience i have i dont think i would have been able to solve that gracefully, considering all the intricacies of everything already animated in the scenes. so you can take this as an advisory against trying to put miles worth of geography into one scene. just separate it

ques: is there any remedy for wanting to do something but ultimately being unable to will yourself to start or continue? sorry if i worded that weirdly

The best way to rescue this is to go back to the exact moment that you realized you wanted it. THAT was what you wanted. it has now somehow evolved into you thinking it's something different, without you realizing it. and that's what's causing all the confusion. going back to the original moment will always give you a refreshed realization of what the desire actually was based on. FOR EXAMPLE, let's say you go to the circus, and you see someone doing something amazing in the circus, and in that moment, you are so captivated and inspired, you feel certain "i want to join the circus!" then as a few days and weeks go by, you don't find yourself joining the circus, you're not even sure how to join the circus, and the whole thing is just a confused haze. But what you must do is, think back to that original moment of inspiration. There was something about what you saw that inspired you deeply, but maybe it's not the element you think. It might just be the person's totally amazing hat. Maybe you just want a cool hat

ques: What is "the click"? I've seen it in a few questions yet ive never really noticed anything prominent like a click sound in your previous songs.
answ: on song production, "the click" refers to the metronome. like a ticking clock, except you set it to the tempo of your song. then you record the song along to it, and it helps everyone stay in time (especially early on, when there's barely anything in the song yet) and it also lets the software know where you are in the song, so it's easy to navigate etc. The metronome itself can never be heard in the final song, you mute it as soon as you have enough percussion and drums to adequately keep the time, but the song will be still be playing to exactly the tempo of the metronome, because that's what you first played the first instruments along to. almost all music recorded after about the year 2000 is on click. which means the tempo stays EXACTLY the same from beginning to end. the whole question is whether that's really a desirable attribute to have

ques: How do I keep up motivation when it comes to learning a language?
answ: "the brain craves repetition and novelty". sameness, but also newness. Some days you just gotta tune into something new. You gotta find new and interesting content. Every now and then you'll remember another one of your hobbies you forgot about, and then you'll search for videos in the language about that. Then you make a new discovery and you go on a binge of transcribing that flies right by because you really like the content and you just wanna know how it turns out. Other times, you crave familiarity, and it's nice to go back to some of the same materials you were dealing with a while back. If it's a transcription, for example, maybe there will be more gaps you'll be able to fill in. this will be rewarding because it will make you feel like you are making progress. ques: in "in the future" why was scene #00352 the best scene
answ: the story behind that scene is this: in the first run-through of making the graphics, that scene looked pretty much exactly like that. And amidst a whole slew of other scenes which i immediately hated, for some reason i really liked that scene. the initial reaction is always what counts, and as i watched what i had, plenty of other scenes i was immediately like "no way" but for that one, my reaction was "oh yes, very good." Then after i did a 2nd and even a 3rd round of fixing and re-doing many of the other scenes, that scene continued to still work for me, but it really seemed like it shouldn't. I'm well aware that we usually don't have any idea why things work or don't, but this scene was particularly perplexing for me because it really seemed like the kind of thing that shouldn't work. And i suppose the insecurity got to me, imagining people looking at that scene and thinking "what the heck dude, it's just a square and a squiggle and nothing's really happening and it just looks like a bunch of loose scraps that kind of aren't doing anything". And yet, i'm always very faithful to my instinctive reaction, which is that it does work very strongly. But i decided what it really needed is some kind of label, to flaunt its confidence as definitely a good scene. just in case anyone else was unsure. and it was also useful that i got to repeat this theme later for another scene

ques: I was also someone who heard romp time from money and got reminded of long long long journey. I think it's because I'm used to trying to find motifs between songs from videogame soundtracks like undertale, and those two melodies would count as a motif between tracks. I get that it wasn't your intention, and that also if this analogy was made from melody into words, it's pretty clear to see how yeah they aren't the same word. I guess what prompted me to push back was that I remember you answered another question about this and said something like "they are entirely different melodies, i guess they both have notes in them." It just feels weird to me since maybe we're not as musically fluent, but let's say someone doesn't know words somehow and they say choose and cheese are the same word. I would probably say they are entirely different words but yeah, I see the similarities, not that they both have letters in them, because of course, I'm pretty sure every word has letters? I guess that was your point, but i felt like either it's not true that some words/melodies are more similar to others, or I'm comparing a melody to another when they have way less similarity than I thought. Could you help me out?
answ: i stand by my theory that no one would make the connection who didn't see it first with the video. the song does not mention 'romp'. you didn't "hear romp time", you "SAW romp time". if you only heard the song and not the video, you'd probably hear it as something like the "not knowing what money means" riff. Because you saw it first with the video, you probably won't be able to un-see it that way. If i find a person who has NEVER seen one of the two videos (they may have seen either one, but not both) and still makes the connection, then this would be a useful counter example. but so far every time someone mentions the connection, they always call it "romp time" which is a dead give away that they saw it first with the video. that is what i believe this hinges around. people hear with their eyes, and see with their ears. i am admittedly not exempt from this
